content.title: [Bug]: Fix multi-line import false positives in diagram generator
content.body:
## Expected behaviour

The diagram generator (`scripts/diagram/ImportExtractor.ts`) correctly identifies all imported names from multi-line import statements, so that `docs/proj-diagram.md` reports only genuinely unused exports.

## Actual behaviour

`extractImportedNames()` uses `lines.find()` to locate the single line containing `from '...'`. For multi-line imports, the matched line is `} from "..."`, which contains no `{...}` destructuring block — so none of the imported names are captured. Every export that is only imported via a multi-line statement is reported as unused.

**False positives observed:** `BurndownResponse`, `BurndownSprintMeta`, `ItemContentType`, all `ports.ts` boundary types, all `queries.ts`/`mappers.ts` exports, all `schemas/scrum.ts` schemas.

**Location:** [`scripts/diagram/ImportExtractor.ts`](scripts/diagram/ImportExtractor.ts)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Locate any file in the project that uses a multi-line import (spread over more than one line)
2. Run the diagram generator
3. Observe that every name from the multi-line import block appears as an "unused export" in `docs/proj-diagram.md`

## Affected MCP tool

Other / unknown — defect is in the `scripts/diagram/` tooling, not the `scrum_*` tool surface.

## Severity

Minor – cosmetic or edge-case issue

---

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Replace single-line `lines.find()` with a loop that collects full multi-line import statements in `extractImportedNames()`
- [ ] Join the collected lines and apply regex on the joined string to handle multi-line imports
- [ ] Run diagram generator and verify false positives are eliminated
- [ ] Regenerate `docs/proj-diagram.md` with accurate unused-export analysis
- [ ] Add unit tests for multi-line import cases

content.body:
## Pre-submission check

## Problem statement

`DependencyPort` declares `findStoryByKey(key: string): Promise<{ status: string | null; title: string } | null>` but has no implementation. `GitHubProjectBackend` does not yet satisfy this contract, leaving `ProjectReader` (which extends `DependencyPort`) incomplete. The dependency enforcement use cases cannot be wired up until this is fulfilled.

## Root cause

The port interface was intentionally written before the adapter implementation (interface-first, as per the project's clean-architecture pattern). The adapter implementation is now the next required step.

## Affected architectural layer

GitHub adapter (src/adapters/github/)

## Risk if deferred

`scrum_get_story` cannot surface resolved dependencies and `scrum_set_field` cannot enforce dependency constraints. Both user stories in the dependency enforcement chain remain blocked.

## Proposed approach

1. Add `findStoryByKey(key: string)` to `GitHubProjectBackend` in `src/adapters/github/backend.ts` (or delegate to an internal service following existing patterns)
2. Normalise the input key: strip leading `#` if present, parse to integer issue number
3. Query the tracked repository for the issue by number; return `{ status, title }` with `status` mapped through `status_display` to the canonical status key; return `null` if the issue is not found or does not belong to the project board
4. Verify `deno check` passes and existing tests are unchanged

- [ ] `GitHubProjectBackend` implements `DependencyPort.findStoryByKey`
- [ ] Keys with and without a leading `#` are both handled correctly
- [ ] A non-existent issue number returns `null` without throwing

content.body:
## Source
[`tasks/REFACTORING.md`](../blob/main/tasks/REFACTORING.md) lines 543–550 (Phase 4 — get-story.ts dependency resolution)

## Context
Phase 4 specifies that `getStoryUseCase` accepts `StoryPort & DependencyPort`, calls `parseDependencies(story.body)`, and resolves `ref.id` via `findStoryByKey()` for entries where `ref.id` is null. The resolved dependencies are included in the `Story` response object.

This ticket adds the concept of a `resolved` boolean on each dependency entry, derived from whether the linked story's status is a terminal status. This is an additive enhancement on top of the Phase 4 specification.

## Scope
- Extend `getStoryUseCase` to accept `StoryPort & DependencyPort`
- Call `parseDependencies(story.body)` to extract dependency entries from the body
- For each dependency where `ref.id` is null, call `backend.findStoryByKey()` to resolve (best-effort; per D7, null ref.id is valid)
- Return a `dependencies` array in the `Story` response: `{ link: { key, kind }, title, status, resolved }`
- `resolved: true` when the linked story's status is a terminal status; `false` otherwise
- `resolved: false` and `status: null` when the linked key cannot be found
- When the story body contains no dependency text, `dependencies` is an empty array
- Existing `story`, `comments`, `linked_prs`, and `acceptance_criteria` fields are unchanged

## Out of scope
- `checkDependenciesUseCase` as a separate use-case (dependency resolution is inline in get-story.ts per Phase 4)
- `DependencyViolationError` and enforcement logic (not in six-phase plan)

- #96 — Dependency domain types (`DependencyEntry`, `blocked_by`/`blocks` on `StoryBase`, `has_dependencies` on `StoryListing`)

content.title: [Story]: Enforce dependency constraints on `scrum_set_field` status mutations
content.body:
## Pre-submission check
- [ ] I have searched existing issues and this story is not already tracked.

## As a…

Team member or agent using `scrum_set_field`

## I want…

The server to reject (or warn) when I try to move a story to a progressing status while it still has unresolved dependencies

## So that…

Work cannot accidentally be started on a story whose declared blockers are still open, keeping the board state accurate without relying solely on human review

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Moving a story to a progressing status (e.g. "Ready", "In Progress", "In Review") when it has at least one unresolved `depends_on` dependency returns an error response listing the unresolved blockers
- [ ] Moving a story to a terminal status ("Done") or a non-progressing status ("Backlog", "Blocked") is never gated by dependency enforcement
- [ ] A story with no dependency links in its body is never affected by enforcement
- [ ] A story whose all declared dependencies are resolved (`status` is terminal) can be moved forward without error
- [ ] The error response includes each unresolved blocker's `key`, `title`, and current `status` so the caller knows exactly what is blocking
- [ ] Enforcement mode defaults to `"error"` until the config option is wired in (see follow-on story)

## Story Point Estimate

3

## Affected component

Use-case layer (src/scrum/)

## Additional context / notes

### Implementation steps
1. Create `src/scrum/set-field.ts` with `setFieldUseCase(reader: StoryPort & DependencyPort, writer: Pick<ProjectWriter, "setField">, ref: StoryRef, field: string, value: unknown, config: SetFieldConfig): Promise<void>`; enforcement fires only when `field === "status"` and `value` is in `config.progressingStatuses`
2. Replace the direct `backend.setField(...)` call in the `scrum_set_field` tool handler (`src/tools/scrum-write.ts`) with `setFieldUseCase`
3. Catch `DependencyViolationError` in the tool handler and return a structured `isError: true` response containing the full blocker list

### Dependencies
- **Depends on:** [Story]: Surface resolved dependencies in `scrum_get_story` response
- **Unblocks:** [Story]: Add `dependency_enforcement` config option

content.body:
## Debt Description

The entire [`src/domain/rules/dependencies.ts`](src/domain/rules/dependencies.ts) module is dead code. All three exports (`parseDependencies`, `hasDependencySection`, `generateDependencySection`) have **zero importers** in the codebase. The adapter layer uses its own `parseDependencies()` in [`src/adapters/github/mappers.ts:43`](src/adapters/github/mappers.ts:43).

The domain version is structurally incompatible with the adapter version — it returns `DependencyEntry[]` (flat list) while the adapter returns `{ blocked_by: DependencyEntry[]; blocks: DependencyEntry[] }` (directional). They cannot be unified by delegation with the current design.

Furthermore, the current dependency implementation relies on ticket body parsing, which is expensive from an API call perspective. The GitHub adapter should utilize the [built-in issue Relationships](https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/using-issues/creating-issue-dependencies) feature.

## Cost of Deferral

- Maintains confusion about which implementation is canonical
- Risk of accidental re-import if a developer searches for `parseDependencies` and finds the domain version first
- 34 lines of dead code to maintain

## Proposed Improvement

Delete the entire file. The adapter's directional format is the canonical one; the domain version has no callers and implements the wrong shape.

Refactor the [`src/adapters/github/internal/resolver.ts`](src/adapters/github/internal/resolver.ts) script to use the `DependencyGraphDependency` type in the GraphQL schema, and pass it over to the upstream abstractions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Remove `src/domain/rules/dependencies.ts`
- [x] `deno lint` passes with no errors
- [x] `deno test` passes
- [x] No other files reference any export from this module (confirmed via search)

- [ ]  [`src/adapters/github/mapper.ts`](src/adapters/github/mapper.ts) resolves item dependencies and relationships

## Notes

## Debt Description

Two related issues share the same root cause:

**Finding 24:** The `has_dependencies` field comment in [`src/scrum/ports.ts:148`](src/scrum/ports.ts:148) says "true when the story body contains a ## Dependencies section" but the actual implementation in `storyToListing` checks `story.blocked_by.length > 0 || story.blocks.length > 0`. content.title: Per-Item Start Dates & Delivery Deadlines with Extension Tracking
content.body:
## User Story

As a developer using the scrum master agent, I want to set a start date and an expected delivery date on any backlog item, so that the agent can flag items that are overdue, prioritize work by approaching deadlines even when the item's priority tier is lower, and always log the reason when a delivery date is pushed out — preserving a full history of every date change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Items can carry a start date (when work is expected to begin) and an expected delivery date (when the item should be Done)
- [ ] The SM agent proactively surfaces overdue items (past their expected delivery date) during every board health check
- [ ] When an item's delivery date is approaching — even if it carries a lower priority tier — the agent flags it as needing attention before higher-priority but later-deadline items
- [ ] Every deadline extension is documented: the agent captures the reason for the delay as a comment on the item before the date field is changed
- [ ] The agent surfaces items with no expected delivery date as a planning gap during refinement and sprint planning

## Non-Goals

- Automatic priority reassignment based on deadlines (the agent can flag tension between deadline urgency and priority tier, but priority is always a human decision)
- Sprint-level deadline enforcement (the sprint end date is tracked separately via burndown)

## As a…
Human using the agent

## I want…
The agent to show me the full dependency picture for a set of items in a single response

- [ ] A sprint with no dependency relationships returns `dependency_map: {}` (empty map), not `null`, when `include_dependencies: true`

## Additional context

Depends on #144. Out-of-scope dependency nodes must carry enough inline state for the agent to make a fetch-or-skip decision without being forced to resolve every node. See `tasks/REFACTORING.md` §"Dependency Graph Pattern" for the full decision table.

content.title: Have `ItemDetailResult` extend `PartialResult` for per-field warning metadata
content.body:
## Problem statement

`ItemDetailResult` has nullable fields (`comments`, `linked_artifacts`) that signal partial completion, but the warnings explaining why those fields are null live on the outer `UseCaseResult.warnings`, not inside the result itself. A consumer holding only an `ItemDetailResult` can't know why data is missing.

[`StoryDetail`](src/scrum/ports.ts:180-184) is already marked deprecated — "Use ItemDetailResult from ../domain/types.ts instead. ItemDetailResult is a superset - it adds acceptance_criteria. StoryDetail will be removed in P2."

## Root cause

`ItemDetailResult` was designed without extending `PartialResult`, so per-field warning metadata is lost when the result is passed to consumers who don't have access to the outer `UseCaseResult`.

## Affected architectural layer

- Domain layer (src/domain/)
- Use-case layer (src/scrum/)

## Risk if deferred

Every consumer of `ItemDetailResult` that needs to explain missing data must also hold the outer `UseCaseResult` — a hidden coupling. This blocks the `StoryDetail` → `ItemDetailResult` migration (P2) and makes error messages to end-users incomplete.

## Proposed approach

1. Add `extends PartialResult` to [`ItemDetailResult`](src/domain/types.ts:577-582)
2. Update [`getStoryUseCase`](src/scrum/get-story.ts) to populate `warnings` inside the `ItemDetailResult` alongside the outer `UseCaseResult`
3. Verify all consumers can access inner warnings

## Done criteria

- [ ] `ItemDetailResult` extends `PartialResult` and inherits the `warnings` field
- [ ] `getStoryUseCase` populates `warnings` inside `ItemDetailResult` with per-field explanations
- [ ] All existing consumers still compile and function correctly
- [ ] A consumer holding just an `ItemDetailResult` can determine why `comments` or `linked_artifacts` is null

## Story Point Estimate

2

## Additional context / related issues

Discovered during implementation of ticket #125 (Move `PartialFailureResult`). Tied to the deprecated `StoryDetail` → `ItemDetailResult` migration.

content.title: [User Story]: Agent receives factual capability statements — NATIVE/EMULATED/UNAVAILABLE for every operation
content.body:
### User Story

As an **agent user**, I want to receive **factual capability statements from the backend** (NATIVE, EMULATED, or UNAVAILABLE for every operation), so that **I know what operations are possible and what limitations apply — without silent degradation**.

### Problem

The current `PlatformCapabilities` uses boolean flags (`canCreateSprints: boolean`). Booleans can't express that an operation works but with emulation constraints. The agent cannot distinguish between "fully supported," "works with limitations," and "impossible."

### Solution

Replace boolean flags with a three-value `CapabilityStatus` enum:
- `NATIVE` — operation maps directly to a platform API call; full fidelity
- `EMULATED` — supported by encoding scrum semantics onto available primitives; constraints apply
- `UNAVAILABLE` — cannot be expressed on this platform

Every field in `PlatformCapabilities` becomes `CapabilityStatus`. Operations with `EMULATED` status must document their emulation contract. `UNAVAILABLE` operations throw `CapabilityUnavailableError` with a `recoverySuggestion`.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `CapabilityStatus` enum replaces booleans in `PlatformCapabilities`
- [ ] `getCapabilities()` returns a `CapabilityMap` derived from the statuses
- [ ] Updating a capability status updates the map automatically — no separate sync needed
- [ ] `EMULATED` operations proceed with a warning appended to `warnings[]`
- [ ] `UNAVAILABLE` operations throw `CapabilityUnavailableError` with `recoverySuggestion`
- [ ] Existing tests pass; new tests cover all three statuses

### Dependencies
None — independent. Can be done in parallel with other streams.

content.title: [User Story]: Agent receives actionable error guidance — BackendError subclasses with recoverySuggestion
content.body:
### User Story

As an **agent user**, I want to receive **actionable error guidance from the backend** (typed `BackendError` subclasses with recovery suggestions), so that **I can recover from errors without seeing raw stack traces or cryptic HTTP status codes**.

### Problem

Raw HTTP/GraphQL errors surface as generic strings or stack traces. The agent can't interpret whether an error is an auth issue (check the token), a rate limit (retry in X seconds), a capability gap (try a different approach), or a platform constraint (results are partial).

### Solution

Implement the error decoration hierarchy:

```
BackendError (base)
BackendAuthError          — token missing/expired → check env var
CapabilityUnavailableError — op can't be expressed → try alternative
CapabilityEmulationWarning — op works with encoding conventions
PlatformConstraintError    — partial/reduced fidelity result
BackendRateLimitError      — retry after X seconds
```

The abstract assembler's `execute()` wrapper catches raw errors from the execution engine and re-throws them as typed `BackendError` subclasses. Each carries a `recoverySuggestion` the agent can surface to the user.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `BackendError` base class with `capability`, `platform`, `recoverySuggestion`, `platformContext` fields
- [ ] All five error subclasses implemented with appropriate `recoverySuggestion` defaults
- [ ] `AbstractAssembler.execute()` wraps raw errors into typed subclasses
- [ ] Use-case functions catch `CapabilityUnavailableError` → surface in `warnings[]`
- [ ] Fatal errors produce structured error strings (not stack traces) in tool responses
- [ ] Agent never sees a raw HTTP status code or GraphQL error

### Dependencies
- [ ] AbstractAssembler implemented
- [ ] CapabilityStatus enum exists

content.title: Impediment: Epic CRUD operations are incomplete
content.body:
## Impediment: Epic CRUD operations are incomplete — no create, no close

### What's Missing

The MCP tool surface offers **no ability to create or close epics (milestones)**. Only read (list/search) and assign-to-story operations exist.

### Layer-by-Layer Gap Analysis

**GraphQL (`operations.graphql`):**
- `ListMilestones` query exists (line 492)
- `SetMilestone` mutation exists (line 832) — assigns an existing milestone to an issue
- No `CreateMilestone` mutation
- No `CloseMilestone` mutation
- No `UpdateMilestone` mutation

**Port interface (`src/scrum/ports.ts`):**
- `EpicPort` (line 292) has only `getEpics()` — single read method
- `ProjectWriter` (line 381) has no epic create/close/update methods
- No `CreateStoryInput`-equivalent for epics (`CreateEpicInput`)

**Adapter (`src/adapters/github/backend.ts`):**
- `getEpics()` delegates to `EpicService` — works for reads
- No `createEpic()` override — `AbstractProjectBackend` doesn't even declare it
- No `closeEpic()` override — same

**Capabilities (`src/adapters/capabilities.ts`):**
- `PlatformCapabilities` has no flag for epic CRUD support (only `auditLogBurndown`, `nativeSprints`, `dependencies`, `fileReader`, `stableItemKeys`)

### Impact

1. Agent must instruct users to create milestones manually in the GitHub UI, then wait for the user to paste the milestone ID back
2. Agent cannot create epics as part of sprint planning
3. Closing a completed epic requires manual GitHub action
4. The just-created "Adapter Layer Assembly Pattern" epic for this project had to be created by the user outside the tool

### Recommended Fix

1. Add `CreateMilestone` and `CloseMilestone` mutations to `operations.graphql`
2. Add `createEpic(input)` and `closeEpic(ref)` to `ProjectWriter` and `EpicPort` ports
3. Implement in `GitHubProjectBackend` via a new method or `EpicService` extension
4. Add MCP tools: `scrum_create_epic(title, description?)` and `scrum_close_epic(ref)`

### Escalation

Day 1 of this impediment. Escalation threshold: Day 2 if no action is taken.

---

## Sub-Impediment: New epics don't appear in `scrum_orient` until they have items in the active sprint

### Root Cause

In `EpicService.getEpics()` (line 50-81), when `sprintIterationId` is `"current"`, the function:
1. Fetches all milestones
2. Fetches items in the active sprint
3. Collects epic IDs that have ≥1 item in the sprint
4. **Filters out milestones NOT in that set**

A newly created milestone with zero items is invisible in `scrum_orient`.

### Impact

- The "Adapter Layer Assembly Pattern" epic doesn't show up in `scrum_orient`'s `epics.active[]` list
- The agent can't verify the epic exists after creation
- Affects any workflow where an epic is created then needs immediate interaction

### Recommended Fix

In `EpicService.getEpics()`: when `sprintIterationId` is `"current"`, return **all open milestones** regardless of sprint item count. The sprint-based filtering should only apply when a specific sprint is requested (not `"current"`). Alternatively, `orientUseCase` in `orient.ts` should call `getEpics(null)` (all milestones) and apply its own `status !== "done"` filter, instead of passing `"current"`.

content.title: [Tech Debt]: Remove silent config fallback — make --config mandatory
content.body:
### Problem

The server silently falls back to `.github/scrum/config.yml` when no `--config` flag or `SCRUM_CONFIG_PATH` env var is provided. When that default path doesn't exist, the server starts in "degraded mode" with stub tools — every tool call returns `"Config not found"` instead of crashing at startup with a clear error.

This masks a genuine configuration error. A developer who starts from the wrong directory or without knowing the flag sees a running process that does nothing useful.

### Diagnosis

**Layer 1 — Server** (`src/server.ts:117-121`): `_configLocation: ContentLocation | undefined` — becomes `undefined` when no config source is provided. The type itself lies (T4 — lying function signature cascade).

**Layer 2 — Adapter** (`src/adapters/github/config-loader.ts:360-363`): `params.configLocation ?? { kind: "file", path: resolve(Deno.cwd(), ".github/scrum/config.yml") }` — a hidden default path.

**Cascade — ConfigReloader** (`src/adapters/github/internal/config-reloader.ts:19`): calls `loadConfig({ github: this.github })` without `configLocation` — will silently break if the `??` fallback is removed without updating this site.

### Impact if not fixed

- **Bad UX:** Server starts without error but every tool fails silently
- **Hidden coupling:** The adapter embeds a default path that only works when CWD is the project root
- **Type debt:** `ContentLocation | undefined` propagates through 5 function/interface signatures where the value is actually always required

### Implementation — 11 sites, 6 files

1. `src/server.ts:114-121` — Add `if (!_rawConfigPath) { console.error(); Deno.exit(1); }`
2. `src/server.ts:78-87` — Help text: remove "(default: .github/scrum/config.yml)", add "(required)"
3. `src/server.ts:245-247` — `createMcpServer(configLocation?:)` → `(configLocation:)`
4. `src/server.ts:262-277` — Simplify error branches (remove dead `else if` / `else`)
5. `src/server.ts:339-341` — `runStdio(configLocation?:)` → `(configLocation:)`
6. `src/server.ts:366` — `runHttp(configLocation?:)` → `(configLocation:)`
7. `src/adapters/factory.ts:18-23` — `AdapterStartupOptions.configLocation` required
8. `src/adapters/github/config-loader.ts:72-77` — `ConfigParams.configLocation` required
9. `src/adapters/github/config-loader.ts:360-363` — Remove `??` fallback
10. `src/adapters/github/internal/config-reloader.ts:12-19` — Add `configLocation` param
11. `src/adapters/github/factory.ts:119` — Pass `configLocation` to `ConfigReloader`

### What stays

- `registerStubTools()` — still needed for `AUTH_FAILED` degraded mode
- `SCRUM_CONFIG_PATH` — still supported (now mandatory)
- The `try/catch` around `createBackend` — needed for other adapter errors

Full plan: `plans/remove-config-fallback.md`

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Server exits with code 1 and clear message when no `--config` or `SCRUM_CONFIG_PATH` set
- [ ] All `ContentLocation | undefined` signatures updated to `ContentLocation` (no lying optionality)
- [ ] `ConfigReloader.reload()` correctly passes the original config location
- [ ] Help text shows `--config` as required
